item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 222315
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Thu Oct 22 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located several hundred miles south-southwest of
Acapulco, Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International
Date Line, a few hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll
late this weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the
system moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 230238
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026
 
...VANCE STRENGTHENING AS IT MOVES NORTHWESTWARD...
...RAPID INTENSIFICATION EXPECTED DURING THE NEXT DAY OR SO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM CST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...10.5N 101.9W
ABOUT 460 MI...745 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 610 MI...980 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...991 MB...29.27 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM CST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was 
located near latitude 10.5 North, longitude 101.9 West. Vance is 
moving toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A gradual turn 
toward the north-northwest is expected over the next day or so. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Rapid intensification is forecast during the next 
24 h, and Vance is forecast to become a major hurricane by early 
Saturday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 991 mb (29.27 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this
weekend and continue into next week. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026 
658 
WTPZ42 KNHC 230239
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Thu Oct 22 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Vance continues to become better 
organized, with an expanding Central Dense Overcast, a well-defined 
curved convective band wrapping into the circulation from the south, 
and cloud-top temperatures as cold as -85 C. Upper-level outflow 
remains well established, and recent microwave imagery reveals an 
improvement in the inner-core structure compared to several hours 
ago. The latest subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was 
T4.0/65 kt, in good agreement with UW-CIMSS objective estimates 
ranging from 55 to 65 kt. Given these estimates and the continued 
improvement in satellite presentation, the initial intensity is 
raised to a conservative 60 kt.

Vance has turned northwestward, and the initial motion is estimated 
at 325/5 kt. The cyclone should continue moving northwestward along 
the southwestern periphery of a mid-level ridge extending over 
Mexico into early Friday. A gradual turn toward the north-northwest 
is expected during the next couple of days as the ridge weakens in 
response to an upper-level trough over the southwestern United 
States. The latest track guidance remains in good agreement through 
about 60 h. Thereafter, the trough is expected to shift eastward, 
leaving Vance in a region of weaker steering currents and resulting 
in increasing spread among the guidance solutions. The regional 
hurricane models and GFS favor a more westward track away from the 
coast between days 4 and 5, while the GDMI, HCCA, TVCN, and ECMWF 
maintain a more north-northwestward track toward the southwestern 
and west-central coast of Mexico. Given these persistent differences 
in the extended guidance, the NHC track forecast is largely 
unchanged from the previous prediction and remains close to the GDMI 
and HCCA aids.

Environmental conditions are expected to remain favorable for 
significant strengthening during the next couple of days, 
characterized by warm sea surface temperatures, low vertical wind 
shear, and plenty of mid-level moisture. Guidance continues to 
indicate a high likelihood of rapid intensification (RI), with 
probabilities from the GFS- and ECMWF-based statistical guidance 
reaching 65 to 80 percent during the next 24 h, well above 
climatological values. Accordingly, the NHC intensity forecast 
explicitly calls for RI during the next 24 h, with Vance forecast to 
become a major hurricane by early Saturday. Thereafter, the cyclone 
could encounter relatively cooler waters, potentially influenced by 
upwelling associated with recent tropical cyclones, along with 
increasing vertical wind shear. These factors should limit further 
strengthening and support gradual weakening beginning around 60 h. 
The NHC intensity forecast is similar to the previous prediction and 
remains near the upper end of the guidance envelope through much of 
the forecast period.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  24/0000Z 11.7N 102.8W   95 KT 110 MPH
